A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLES research, authors, control benchmarks and policy examples. The main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Lunar Lander and Car Racing experiments, policy-ensemble results, and behavioral-evidence and prompt comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds component ablations, runtime measurements, policy-population heatmaps and feedback from 20 graduate students.

M1.justification: Reported parent selection changes from p_i proportional to 1/(r_i+N) in v1 Section 3.4 to exponential selection, exp(-c r_i), in v2 Section 2.4. The policy representation, four evolutionary operators, behavioral-evidence construction and example policy code remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Control-task coverage remains Lunar Lander and Car Racing. v2 Section 3.2 adds an informal human-readability evaluation involving 20 computer-science graduate students, introducing a participant population and evaluation task absent from v1.

E2.justification: The benchmark baselines remain DQN, PPO, EoH and the initial policy. v2 Tables 2 and 10 add internal comparison variants removing individual operators, operator pairs or Thought. Genetic programming and policy distillation are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds a substantial evaluation protocol for total runtime and time to thresholds of 1.00 and 95.0, using GPU-assisted DRL and eight-process LES execution in Appendix B.2. It also introduces component-removal controls and human code review. The existing benchmark splits, reset budgets, metrics and network configurations are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing evidence-format and prompt analyses, v2 adds ablations of all four operators individually, both operator groups and Thought, testing their contributions and interaction. Appendix B.5 adds per-policy, per-instance heatmaps examining complementary strengths. The earlier ensemble experiment is retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 specifies three independent runs for the new ablation variants. Existing five-run benchmark and prompt experiments remain. Training SEM and best-run results were already reported in v1 Table 8; their inclusion in v2 Table 1 is relocation, not first-time uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds ablation outcomes, population heatmaps, participant feedback and runtime results; its new timing study reports Car Racing time to threshold of 3h16min for MLES versus 12h for PPO. Most earlier results are retained. However, MLES's Car Racing training mean changes from 98.704 to 98.070 in Table 1, while v2 Table 11 still reports 98.704; this discrepancy is unexplained.

T1.justification: The formal parent-selection probability changes from an inverse-rank expression to exponential rank decay. The policy-discovery optimization objective and normalized weight score definition are unchanged, and neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of direct programmatic policy discovery, transparent control logic and PPO-comparable performance persist. v2's abstract and conclusion narrow their explicit PPO comparison to performance, omitting v1's accompanying claim of comparable policy-discovery efficiency.

C2.justification: v1 identifies higher computational cost than DRL as a limitation; v2 replaces this with a favorable cost-benefit argument citing approximately USD 0.42 for Car Racing. v2 also adds explanations of task-dependent operator contributions, runtime advantages and complementary policy strengths. Its blanket claim that full MLES outperforms every ablation conflicts with the reported Lunar Lander result without E1.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents API-based inference, eight-process sampling and evaluation, RTX 4060 use for the timing study, and measured time and financial costs. Existing hyperparameter tables, network architectures, prompt templates and policy code remain available; no new code-access resource is provided.

R1.justification: v2 condenses related-work coverage, removing finite-state-policy discussion and several tree-policy citations, and adds Blickle and Thiele (1996) for selection schemes. It adds reasons for excluding genetic-programming and distillation baselines while retaining the main positioning around direct policy synthesis with multimodal evolutionary search.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and reorganizes the narrative: related work moves after experiments, ensemble analysis moves into Appendix B.5, and experimental appendices precede metric and evidence descriptions. The title changes, IBE becomes BE, and interpretability terminology is broadly revised toward transparency and human readability. A manuscript LLM-use disclosure is added.

P2.justification: The main document changes from two-column to single-column presentation. Figure 1 is redesigned, Table 1 incorporates the earlier appendix statistics, and pseudocode, ablation tables, a runtime table and population heatmaps are added. Existing convergence plots, ensemble results, prompts and policy examples are relocated or reformatted rather than removed.

improvement.justification: The component ablations and runtime measurements provide useful evidence absent from v1, strengthening assessment of MLES's mechanisms and practical efficiency. The informal readability review adds limited support for transparency claims. These gains are tempered by the inconsistent Car Racing mean in v2 Tables 1 and 11 and the overstatement that full MLES beats every ablation despite the contrary Lunar Lander entry in Table 10.
